_readme:
THE MODEL MANIFEST (card MDL-1, 2026-09-01). DEFINITIONS ONLY — this file IS the product; there is no engine and no emitted plane. One entry per model in use today, answering three questions in one place: what does it cost, what key does it spend, and is it approved. DATA, NEVER CODE — edit and commit, and the next consumer that reads it sees the change; no restart, no code change.

KEY NAMES, NEVER KEY VALUES. `key_env` is the NAME of an environment variable and nothing else. `validate.py` refuses a value-shaped `key_env` by shape (see _field_notes.key_env) so a pasted secret fails the manifest loudly instead of riding into git.

EVERYTHING SEEDS AS `draft`. Rule 6 of components/CLAUDE.md: the definition owner holds the approval gate. Curator is the developer; nothing here is `approved` until he says so, and a consumer that only runs approved models will find this file empty until then — deliberately.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT HERE. Seeded from the two fragments MDL-1 was pointed at: the chain-runner's video-teardown chain.json model bindings, and the bench menu at new-workflow-design/builds/chain-qa/bench-models.json. NOT folded in yet, and each named so the hole is visible rather than silent: (fragment) the mini-worker's fal IMAGE menu (platform/workers/mini-worker/models.json + prices.json — 17 endpoints WITH real billed prices, the only priced model data the org has), (fragment) the atlas's hand-drawn model nodes, (fragment) the bench's `chain-head` arm, which is NOT a model at all (it is the chain's own runner inside the pinned clone) and should never gain an entry here. Each folds in under its own MDL-2 card, never one big-bang rewire. LETTERING NOTE (2026-09-01, batch-20 finding 4): the CARD's lettering is authoritative — MDL-2 (a) bench-models.json, (b) chain.json bindings, (c) atlas manual nodes, (d) lora.json emits, (e) the worker's fal image menu (models.json + prices.json — ruled in 2026-09-01). An earlier local (a)(b)(c) here named a different list and is neutralized above.

_field_notes.id: The registry's canonical name for the model. Lowercase, id-shaped. This is the name a consumer should migrate TO. Unique across the file — including against every `aliases` entry.
_field_notes.aliases: Other names the same model already answers to in code that landed before this registry existed. The chain-runner's seam ids (`opus`, …) are pattern-routed in components/chain-runner/runner/vendors.py and predate the registry — the CR-2b rider flagged exactly this. Listed here so MDL-2 (b) is a migration, not an archaeology exercise.
_field_notes.modality: A LIST, because a model is not one thing: gemini-3-flash-preview is bound to video stages AND a text stage in the same chain. Closed vocabulary: text, image, video, audio.
_field_notes.cost: EITHER the literal string "unpriced" — which REQUIRES `cost_reason` in words — OR an object of named numeric USD rates. Token models use explicit per-million names for every priced class the source exposes: `usd_per_1m_input`, `usd_per_1m_output`, and, when known, `usd_per_1m_reasoning`, `usd_per_1m_cache_read`, `usd_per_1m_cache_write`. An absent class is unknown, never zero. A bare number is refused (no unit = no answer), and a rate of 0 also requires `cost_reason`. This is the bench's own doctrine held as a schema rule: a zero and an unknown are different answers, and $__ is the one nobody may show for a model whose spend was never measured.
_field_notes.status: draft | approved | deprecated (components/CLAUDE.md rule 6). The definition owner's gate. Seeded draft.
_field_notes.key_env: The NAME of the environment variable the model spends, or null when it spends none. null means the model runs on a login rather than a key — the claude CLI's own — so there is no key to name. Shape-enforced: ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,23}$ and no run of 3+ digits, which is what makes a pasted key value fail.
_field_notes.transport: claude-cli | api | local — how the call actually leaves the machine. It is why `key_env` is null for the claude family, and it is a real cost fact: the CLI measures no per-run spend. `local` means the weights run on our own machine and the call never leaves it, so `key_env` must be null (a key name on a local entry is refused) and its zero rate carries a `cost_reason` (SI-172 (model id drafts)).
_field_notes.sources: Where this entry was read off. Provenance, so a curator can check the seed rather than trust it.
_field_notes.request: OPTIONAL. The REQUEST-LEVEL CONTROLS this entry declares, in the vendor's own spelling, because the consumer puts them on the request body UNCHANGED. Two controls and no more: `reasoning` ({effort, max_tokens, exclude, enabled, context, mode} — effort and max_tokens are mutually exclusive) and `provider` ({order, allow_fallbacks}). AN ENTRY THAT DECLARES NO `request` PRODUCES TODAY'S PAYLOAD BYTE FOR BYTE — the absence is the answer and there is no default to inherit. WHY IT EXISTS: on 2026-09-09 the identical request to deepseek-v4-flash-0731 ran twice at max_tokens 16000 and differed BY ROUTE — through Relace it stopped on `length` with 0 characters after 59,707 characters of hidden reasoning; through OpenInference it ANSWERED. The budget was never the lever. Pinning removes failover, so it is never assumed: an entry that wants a deterministic route says `allow_fallbacks: false` itself. Added MDL-5 (reasoning budget), 2026-09-09.
_field_notes.default_max_tokens: OPTIONAL. The output budget a request that names none inherits FOR THIS MODEL. A text model spends its output budget on output; a reasoning model spends an unbounded prefix of it on thinking the caller never sees, so one global default cannot be right for both. The consumer's own ceiling still applies (`max_tokens_cap`) and is never raised to fit an entry; a request's own `max_tokens` still wins over this. Added MDL-5 (reasoning budget), 2026-09-09.
_field_notes.vendor_id: The name the VENDOR answers to, when it differs from the registry `id` — an OpenRouter id carries a slash (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`), which the id shape (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$) forbids, and the registry's own name is what a consumer keys on. A consumer that makes the call sends `vendor_id` to the vendor and never a free-text string of its own; when absent, `id` IS the vendor's name. Added MDL-4 (openrouter vendor), 2026-09-09.

models.label: GLM 5.3 Flash (via OpenRouter)
models.cost_reason: RE-SWEPT 2026-10-11T06:34Z by the dev-developer lead, read from OpenRouter's public list (GET /api/v1/models, no key), never relayed: input 0.15, output 0.5, cache read 0.03 USD per 1M — was 0.075/0.25. EARLIER READING: OpenRouter's public model list (GET /api/v1/models, read 2026-09-09T04:33Z, no key): prompt 0.000000075 USD/token, completion 0.00000025 USD/token, context 1,310,720. The rate is OpenRouter's list price, billed per call against OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the true spend per call is what the vendor's usage block reports and the infer record carries it. Re-read the list when a price looks stale — this is data, never a promise. BATCH LANE, checked 2026-09-15 in the same sweep: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:batch` costs EXACTLY THE SAME as interactive — $__/$__, cache read identical. It is not cheaper and not dearer. What it DOES buy is a max_completion_tokens of 943,718 against this row's 131,072, for a smaller context (1,048,576 against 1,310,720). So on this model a batch lane is a LENGTH decision, not a price one — which is worth knowing before anyone reaches for batch expecting a discount.
models._request_note: NO REQUEST CONTROLS AT ALL, AND `reasoning` WAS REMOVED ON 2026-09-10 BECAUSE THE VENDOR REFUSES IT. MDL-5 (reasoning budget) set `reasoning.enabled: false` here on the reading that it is the one knob every model supports. This endpoint says otherwise, in so many words: HTTP 400, "Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled" (probe-glm-real, 2026-09-10T00:33:06Z). So the control did not merely fail to bound anything — IT BROKE EVERY CALL, turning a wasteful 200 into a hard 400. Removed so the entry works again at yesterday's behaviour. THAT BEHAVIOUR IS STILL NOT GOOD: this model has returned 0 characters through Novita, DigitalOcean and Z.AI at max_tokens 16000, spending the whole budget on reasoning it will not let us turn off. NO PROVIDER PIN, because no upstream has ever answered it with characters and inventing one would be a guess the registry does not make. The open question is whether a budget large enough for reasoning AND an answer exists at a price worth paying — carded as MDL-6 (glm reasoning mandatory), and until it is answered this entry is approved but useless.
models.note: THE FIRST STANDING INFERENCE VENDOR — the text parallel to fal.ai for images (the developer, 2026-09-09: "a parallel to fal.ai but for inference models … include it in the models component to be used more generally"). One of the two outside reviewers the model-stack pilot names. Z.ai's own endpoint is marked Private on OpenRouter (batch 80). Reached only through the worker's `infer` action (WM-34 (infer action)) under the scoped grant; no other OpenRouter client exists in the org. DRAFT until the curator blesses it — that is the gate, not a placeholder.

models.label: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731, via OpenRouter)
models.cost_reason: RE-SWEPT 2026-10-11T06:34Z by the dev-developer lead, read from OpenRouter's public list (GET /api/v1/models, no key), never relayed: input 0.0175, output 0.64, cache read 0.0175 USD per 1M — was 0.06/0.12. EARLIER READING: RE-READ AND CORRECTED 2026-09-15 by the lead, sweeping every openrouter row against the live list: prompt 0.00000006, completion 0.00000012 — $__/M in and $__/M out. THE ROW HAD $__/$__, read on 2026-09-09; the output rate has fallen 33% since. Nothing was wrong when it was filed — A PRICE IS A READING WITH A DATE ON IT, and this row proves a registry row goes stale on its own, with no edit and no mistake. Every cost comparison run against this row between 09-09 and now OVERSTATED DeepSeek 0731 by a third on output. The 09-09 reading is kept here rather than erased: 'prompt 0.000000065, completion 0.00000018, context 1,310,720; DISAGREES with the per-provider figure read in the browser the same day (batch 80: $__/M in, $__/M out) — that was one provider's rate, the list price is the model's headline.' No time-of-day overrides on this id, checked in the same sweep. Billed per call against OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the infer record carries what the vendor's usage block reports.
models._request_note: PINNED TO ONE UPSTREAM, FALLBACKS OFF, ON ONE MEASURED SUCCESS. The identical request ran twice on 2026-09-09 at max_tokens 16000 and differed by ROUTE: through Relace it returned finish_reason `length`, 0 characters of reply, 59,707 characters of hidden reasoning, $__ spent for nothing; through OpenInference it returned finish_reason `stop` and 2,087 characters of ANSWER on near-identical reasoning volume. So the budget is survivable and the ROUTE decides — which is why fallbacks are off: a gate that passes on a lucky route tests nothing. The evidence is ONE success and is thin. THE SLUG IS THE NAME THE VENDOR REPORTED BACK on that record (`provider: OpenInference`); it was NOT checked against OpenRouter's provider-slug list, which needs network the maker had none of. If the slug is wrong the pin fails CLOSED — a refusal naming it, never a silent reroute. `reasoning.enabled: false` may bound nothing on this vendor (effort is OpenAI/Grok, reasoning.max_tokens is Anthropic/Gemini); it is sent so the probe is a bounded one, never as proof. MDL-5 (reasoning budget), 2026-09-09.
models.note: The second outside reviewer the model-stack pilot names. DATA-POLICY FACT: DeepSeek's first-party endpoint TRAINS on prompts (batch 80); the account's data policy excludes training providers (the developer's click, batch 100), so whether a non-training provider serves this id under that policy is UNCHECKED until the infer action's first call — a `no provider` refusal on that call is the answer, and this entry comes out rather than the policy loosening (MDL-4 (openrouter vendor) kill-condition). The dated id pins the snapshot; `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (undated) also exists on the list and is deliberately not the one recorded. DRAFT until the curator blesses it.

models.label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (via OpenRouter)
models.cost_reason: RE-SWEPT 2026-10-11T06:34Z by the dev-developer lead, read from OpenRouter's public list (GET /api/v1/models, no key), never relayed: input 0.3, output 1.2, cache read 0.006 USD per 1M — was 0.15/0.6. The headline rate now equals the old weekday-peak rate, read on a Sunday — the base itself has doubled. EARLIER READING: OpenRouter's public model list (GET /api/v1/models, no key), READ AND VERIFIED BY THE LEAD 2026-09-15T15:34Z, not relayed: prompt 0.00000015, completion 0.0000006 USD/token; context 1,048,576; max_completion_tokens 384,000; input modalities text+image; created 2026-09-10T06:21:25Z. THE HEADLINE RATE IS NOT WHAT WE WOULD PAY, and the list says so: this model carries TIME-OF-DAY PRICING OVERRIDES. Monday-Friday 01:00-04:00Z and 06:00-10:00Z the rate DOUBLES to prompt 0.0000003 / completion 0.0000012 (i.e. $__ and $__ per 1M). Weekends and all other hours are the base rate above. Our own scheduled work sits inside BOTH peak windows - the 03:13Z nightly QC sweep and the ~06:40-10:00Z verifier runs - so a measured pair scheduled the way today's jobs are scheduled would be billed at 2x the figure in `cost`, and a cost comparison against a flat-rate model is wrong by that factor unless it is run outside those hours or the doubling is stated. Cache reads are 0.000000003 ($__ per 1M), cheap enough to change how a repeated-context judge is designed. Billed per call against OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the infer record carries what the vendor's usage block reports.

OpenRouter GET /api/v1/models, read by the lead 2026-09-16T05:20Z (443 models on the list)
models.note: An ARM for the design bench (DB-1 (bench runner)). FILED `draft` DELIBERATELY: rule 6 seeds draft and the developer is the registry's curator, so "set up the registry" is read as an instruction to CREATE the rows, not to pass his own approval gate — he flips it in one word. Nothing is blocked meanwhile: the bench's OpenRouter arms run on a draft row via `allow_draft` on the request record. COST IN CONTEXT, which is the whole reason DB-1 (bench runner) takes a ROUTE PER ARM: a ~10k-token mock costs about $__ here versus $__ on the subscription route for the same family.
